subject: Equinox Labs: Dedicated capacity planning and transient-reserve orchestration
messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity planning for Equinox - anticipated traffic profile

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. A few follow-ups from our infra team so we can size a Dedicated deployment and figure out transient capacity patterns. High level:
- Goal: GA by Q3; pilot in June.
- Peak concurrency: ~480-600 concurrent inference sessions (token streaming), median seq length ~512, p95 token length ~1024.
- Acceptable p95 latency for interactive flows: <= 350ms on 1xA100-class GPU.
- We expect regular weekday spikes tied to batch reprocessing windows (1–2 hours) plus irregular customer events.

Specific asks:
1) How do you recommend mixing reserved slabs with transient/warm pools for this profile?
2) What's Redwood's autoscale grace / cooldown guidance to avoid oscillation for short spikes?
3) If we allow preemptible (opportunistic) capacity, what are the fallback behaviors you recommend (model variant, hosted fallback, throttling)?

I'll loop in Claire (PM) after this thread. Can we get a short runbook + a capacity matrix you can use for pricing?

Thanks,
Eric Barker
Head of Platform
Equinox Labs

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for Equinox - anticipated traffic profile

Eric — thanks, this is really helpful. I've attached a capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx and a short draft MOP (draft_mop_equinox.pdf) that sketches an initial approach. High-level proposal:

- Reserved baseline: size for sustained concurrency (we recommend planning for ~60% of your reported weekday steady state). For your numbers that maps to ~300 concurrent inference sessions as the committed slab.
- Ephemeral shoulder pool: a warm pool of pre-warmed instances that can absorb 20–30% short spikes with <200ms warm-up added latency. This pool runs as reserved-but-scaled (lower-priority) so it stays warm for predictable spikes.
- Opportunistic preemptibles: separate pool of cheaper preemptible GPUs for deep bursts; these should be used with graceful degradation: 1) automatic fallback to a quantized / smaller model variant, 2) fallback to hosted Redwood API for low-priority traffic, or 3) circuit-breaker thinning for non-interactive jobs.

Autoscale policy recommendations (draft):
- Scale-up: immediate + additive policy for rapid ramp (trigger at sustained 3s average above threshold); allow up to 2x within 5 minutes (fast path).
- Scale-down: conservative cooldown (15-30m) to avoid thrash for brief spikes. Use moving median of 5m / 15m windows to discriminate tails.
- Headroom: keep 12–18% idle headroom in the reserved pool for KV cache warmness and routing overhead.

I've asked Rishi and Karthik to validate the model selection implications and any runtime constraints. Next step: internal sizing alignment and then a short call with your infra team Monday/Tuesday.

Thanks,

Nikhil / all — quick technical notes and a slightly different headroom suggestion based on their token lengths and streaming workload.

On Fri, Mar 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Headroom: keep 12–18% idle headroom in the reserved pool for KV cache warmness and routing overhead.

That range is fine for most LLM chat workloads, but given: (a) p95 seq length ~1024 and (b) streaming sessions have high burstiness, I suggest we recommend a tiered headroom approach in the MOP:
- Cold start buffer: 20% for first 60 minutes after deployment or after a major model change.
- Steady-state buffer: 12% for normal days.
- Event buffer: temporary +30% applied only during scheduled event windows (1–2 hours) controlled by a manual override in the console.

Autoscale tuning:
- Use continuous batching window of 50–200ms to improve throughput during high token-per-second phases; that reduces GPU churn.
- Fast-path scale-up: allow pre-warmed shoulder nodes to be brought online within 60–90s by keeping a small number of nodes in idle-but-reserved state (we call these warm-warm).
- Preemption plan: if preemptible nodes are reclaimed, route affected sessions to quantized model on dedicated pool for 95% of cases; only if saturated fallback to hosted API (with rate limiting tags).

I'll add a short runbook snippet (runbook_snippet.txt) showing the exact console toggles and the manual override process.

-Rishi
